Pattapu θōka retains the long vowel and medial k, with an initial dental fricative in place of the comparanda’s stop; the transcription remains unchanged. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. proposals.evidence: DEDR1481: Tamil/Malayalam kāṟṟu, Kota ka·ṯ and Kodagu ka·tï denote wind. Pattapu kāθu preserves the long-vowel k-initial stem with a dental fricative corresponding to the dental/alveolar stop series. The article’s kāl noun belongs to this same family and does not require changing the displayed head. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. proposals.evidence: DEDR2146: Tamil koḻuppu denotes fat and grease; Malayalam koḻuppu denotes fatness and solidity of broth or curry. Pattapu kolupu preserves this suffixed noun with plain l and single p in the source; it is compared with the attested noun rather than assigned an invented synchronic derivation. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1693: Telugu guṇḍe-kāya, Tulu guṇḍe-kāyi and Kannada guṇḍi-kāyi explicitly denote the physical heart. Pattapu guⁿdekāi matches this full formation. Ordered components are DEDR1693 heart/chest plus DEDR1459 kāy/kāya/kāyi fruit/nut; the latter also includes Kodagu kāy kidneys. Source nasal notation and final diphthong are retained. These are component links, not two alternative whole-word etymologies. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3684: Tamil/Malayalam nī and Kodagu nī/nīnï are second-person singular pronouns. Pattapu niyi is proposed as the corresponding stem with a glide and final vowel; its short vowels are retained. The two source records specify female and male addressees but have identical forms, so both records remain distinct without inventing a morphological gender contrast. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
